\section[frequentemente]{frequentemente — frequently, often}

\label{lesson:PT-C277-frequentemente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the millennium, then the Portuguese for subsequent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: frequentemente}
\textbf{frequentemente} — \textquotedblleft{}frequently, often\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Vou frequentemente ao cinema.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I often go to the cinema.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Muitas vezes} is the everyday way to say it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{frequentemente} is built on \emph{frequente}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{frequēns} \textquotedblleft{}crowded, frequent\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), with the ending \emph{-mente}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{frequentemente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{frequentemente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{frequentemente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the millennium, then the Portuguese for subsequent, then say \emph{frequentemente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does frequentemente mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Frequently, often\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ocasionalmente]{ocasionalmente — occasionally, now and then}

\label{lesson:PT-C277-ocasionalmente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for subsequent, then the Portuguese for frequently.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: ocasionalmente}
\textbf{ocasionalmente} — \textquotedblleft{}occasionally, now and then\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ocasionalmente, jantamos fora.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Now and then we eat out.}
\end{quote}

Close to \emph{de vez em quando}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ocasionalmente} is built on \emph{ocasião} \textquotedblleft{}occasion\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{occāsiō} \textquotedblleft{}a fitting moment, a chance\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{occidere} \textquotedblleft{}to fall\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{cadere}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[habitualmente]{habitualmente — usually, habitually}

\label{lesson:PT-C277-habitualmente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for frequently, then the Portuguese for occasionally.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: habitualmente}
\textbf{habitualmente} — \textquotedblleft{}usually, habitually\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Habitualmente, almoço na cantina.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I usually have lunch in the canteen.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Normalmente} means much the same.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{habitualmente} is built on \emph{habitual} (EtymDB), from Latin \emph{habitus} \textquotedblleft{}condition, habit\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{habēre} \textquotedblleft{}to have, to hold\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[diariamente]{diariamente — daily, every day}

\label{lesson:PT-C277-diariamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for occasionally, then the Portuguese for usually.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: diariamente}
\textbf{diariamente} — \textquotedblleft{}daily, every day\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O jornal chega diariamente às oito horas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The newspaper arrives every day at eight.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Todos os dias} is the everyday way to say it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{diariamente} is built on \emph{diário} \textquotedblleft{}daily\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{diārium} \textquotedblleft{}a daily allowance\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{diēs} \textquotedblleft{}day\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[previamente]{previamente — beforehand, in advance}

\label{lesson:PT-C277-previamente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for usually, then the Portuguese for daily.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: previamente}
\textbf{previamente} — \textquotedblleft{}beforehand, in advance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
É preciso marcar a visita previamente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{You need to book the visit in advance.}
\end{quote}

Formal; in speech, \emph{antes} or \emph{com antecedência}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{previamente} is built on \emph{prévio} \textquotedblleft{}prior\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from Latin \emph{praevius} \textquotedblleft{}going before\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{prae} \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{} and \emph{via} \textquotedblleft{}way\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
